sections.title: An arrow and a list
beats: A vector is an arrow with a length and a direction.
It's also just a list of numbers. [3, 2] means 3 right, 2 up.
Physics sees arrows, computer science sees lists, math says both are the same thing.
sections.example: Your portfolio is a vector: [BTC units, ETH units, SOL units].

quiz.q: What does [−1, 4] mean as an arrow?

sections.title: Adding & scaling
beats: Scaling multiplies every number: 2×[1,2] = [2,4]. Same direction, twice as long.
A negative scale flips the direction.
sections.example: Two trades' position changes add up into your net position change.
sections.sayback: Show adding two arrows on paper.
sections.tieback: Liquid Bot: exposure across assets is a vector. A cap on open positions is a limit on it.
